vectors.name: IRQ0 timer tick
vectors.detail: Hardware interrupt from PIT counter 0 (18.2 Hz). The BIOS handler counts ticks at 40:6C, runs the floppy motor timeout, calls INT 1Ch and sends the EOI.
quirks: Never call it with int: it sends an EOI to the PIC for an interrupt that was not delivered.
Vector 08h is also CPU exception #DF in protected mode; remap the PIC before enabling interrupts there.

vectors.name: Video services
quirks: Some older BIOSes destroy BP (and, rarely, SI/DI) across video calls, notably scroll (AH=06h/07h) and teletype (AH=0Eh); save what must survive.
Video BIOS code may use 32-bit registers without preserving the high halves on some cards.

vectors.name: Disk services
quirks: DL: 00h-7Fh floppy, 80h and up hard disk (or emulated drive). The boot drive number arrives in DL at 0000:7C00; save it before anything clobbers DL.
Floppy operations may fail the first time while the motor spins up: reset (AH=00h) and retry three times.
The handler enables interrupts while waiting for the drive.

vectors.name: System services
quirks: Handlers may return with interrupts enabled even when called with IF clear; re-execute cli after the call in a critical section.
AH=86h (unsupported function) in AH with CF set is the usual not-supported answer, but some BIOSes return 80h.

vectors.name: User timer tick hook
vectors.detail: Called by the INT 08h handler on every tick; the default handler is a bare iret.
quirks: A hook must be short, chain to the previous handler and preserve every register; it runs before the timer EOI is sent, so lower-priority IRQs are blocked meanwhile.

structs.name: dap
structs.title: Disk address packet (INT 13h AH=42h/43h/44h)

fields.name: size
fields.desc: packet size: 10h, or 18h with the 64-bit buffer address

fields.name: count
fields.desc: blocks to transfer (in: requested; out: done). Many BIOSes allow at most 127 (7Fh)

fields.name: segment
fields.desc: buffer segment; FFFF:FFFF selects the 64-bit address at offset 16

notes: The packet and the buffer must be addressable in real mode (below 1 MiB), and DS:SI points at the packet.

structs.name: e820
structs.title: E820h address range descriptor

fields.name: length
fields.desc: length in bytes; skip zero-length entries

fields.name: type
fields.desc: 1 usable RAM, 2 reserved, 3 ACPI reclaimable, 4 ACPI NVS, 5 bad memory; treat anything else as reserved

fields.name: attributes
fields.desc: ACPI 3.0 extended attributes: bit 0 = entry valid (ignore the entry when clear), bit 1 = non-volatile

notes: Pass ECX = 24 and pre-set the attributes dword to 1, so a BIOS that writes only 20 bytes still yields a valid entry.

structs.name: edd-params
structs.title: EDD drive parameters (INT 13h AH=48h)

fields.name: size
fields.desc: in: buffer size (1Ah EDD 1.x, 1Eh EDD 2.x, 42h EDD 3.0, 4Ah T13 EDD-3); out: bytes filled

fields.name: flags
fields.desc: bit 0 DMA boundary errors handled, 1 CHS info valid, 2 removable, 3 write verify, 4 change line, 5 lockable, 6 CHS set to max

fields.name: dpte
fields.desc: far pointer to the device parameter table extension; FFFF:FFFF = none

fields.name: key
fields.desc: BEDDh when the device path fields are valid

fields.name: path_length
fields.desc: device path information length including the key: 24h (Phoenix EDD 3.0) or 2Ch (T13 EDD-3)

fields.name: interface
fields.desc: interface type, ASCII: "ATA", "ATAPI", "SCSI", "USB", "1394", "FIBRE" padded with spaces

fields.name: device_path
fields.desc: interface-specific device (ATA: master/slave); 16 bytes in T13 EDD-3

notes: Set the size word before the call. Phoenix EDD 3.0 ends at 42h with a checksum at 41h; T13 EDD-3 widens the device path to 16 bytes and ends at 4Ah.
Some BIOSes return 0 bytes per sector or bogus geometry for USB devices; trust the total sector count first.

structs.name: cdrom-spec
structs.title: El Torito specification packet (INT 13h AH=4Bh)

fields.name: media
fields.desc: boot media type: bits 3:0 0 no emulation, 1 1.2M floppy, 2 1.44M, 3 2.88M, 4 hard disk

fields.name: drive
fields.desc: drive number the image is emulated as

fields.name: image_lba
fields.desc: LBA of the disk image being emulated

fields.name: device_spec
fields.desc: device specification (IDE master/slave, SCSI LUN and ID)

fields.name: buffer_segment
fields.desc: segment of the 3K read cache buffer

fields.name: cyl_low
fields.desc: low 8 bits of cylinder count (INT 13h AH=08h CH)

fields.name: sec_cyl_high
fields.desc: sector count and cylinder bits 9:8 (AH=08h CL)

notes: Layout from the El Torito specification; several BIOSes fill only the first few bytes for no-emulation boots.

structs.name: move-gdt
structs.title: INT 15h AH=87h block move descriptor table

fields.name: source
fields.desc: source data descriptor: limit 15:0 (at least 2*CX-1), base 23:0, access 93h, then limit/flags and base 31:24 (zero on a 286)

notes: Base bits 31:24 at descriptor byte 7 are honoured by 386+ BIOSes only; 286-era BIOSes reach 16 MiB at most.

structs.name: vbe-info
structs.title: VBE controller information (INT 10h AX=4F00h)

fields.name: signature
fields.desc: out: "VESA"; set "VBE2" on input to receive VBE 2.0+ fields

fields.name: oem_string
fields.desc: far pointer to the OEM string

fields.name: capabilities
fields.desc: bit 0 DAC width switchable, 1 not VGA compatible, 2 RAMDAC blank bit

fields.name: mode_list
fields.desc: far pointer to the mode list, FFFFh-terminated words; may point into this buffer

notes: Copy the mode list before the next VBE call: it can live in the scratch area of this buffer.

fields.name: attributes
fields.desc: bit 0 supported, 3 colour, 4 graphics, 7 linear framebuffer available

fields.name: win_func
fields.desc: far pointer to the bank switch function

fields.name: pitch
fields.desc: bytes per scan line (banked modes; VBE 3.0 has a separate linear pitch)

fields.name: framebuffer
fields.desc: physical address of the linear framebuffer (VBE 2.0+)

structs.name: sysconf
structs.title: System configuration table (INT 15h AH=C0h)

fields.name: feature1
fields.desc: bit 1 Micro Channel, 2 EBDA allocated, 4 INT 15h AH=4Fh called by INT 09h, 5 RTC present, 6 second 8259 present

notes: The table is in ROM; read only.

services.name: Set video mode
in: mode (bit 7 set = do not clear the screen); 03h = 80x25 colour text, 13h = 320x200x256

services.name: Get cursor position and shape
quirks: Phoenix BIOSes also return AX = 0.

services.name: Scroll window up
quirks: Some IBM-compatible BIOSes destroy BP (and DS on a few); save both.
services.confidence: BP/DS destruction is reported for specific old BIOSes only

services.name: Scroll window down
quirks: Same BP caveat as AH=06h.

services.name: Read character and attribute at cursor
Write character and attribute at cursor
quirks: Does not move the cursor and does not interpret CR, LF or BS.

services.name: Write character at cursor
quirks: Keeps the existing attribute; does not move the cursor.

services.name: Teletype output
quirks: Interprets BEL, BS, CR and LF and scrolls at the bottom; LF does not imply CR.
Some old BIOSes destroy BP; save it.

services.name: Write string
in: mode: bit 0 update cursor, bit 1 string holds char,attr pairs
quirks: Not on the original PC and XT BIOSes.
BP is an input here, so code that relies on BP as a frame pointer must reload it.

services.name: VBE get controller information
services.errNote: AL = 4Fh means the function exists; AH = 00h success, else the status code.

services.name: VBE set mode
in: mode: bit 14 linear framebuffer, bit 15 keep memory, bit 11 use CRTC info at ES:DI (VBE 3.0)
quirks: Check mode-info attribute bit 7 before setting bit 14.

services.name: Get conventional memory size
out: KiB of memory from 0 (40:13), typically 639 or less with an EBDA
quirks: The value excludes the EBDA; memory between AX*1024 and 0xA0000 belongs to the BIOS.

services.name: Get status of last operation
out: status of the last operation on the drive
services.errNote: CF is set when the status is not zero on most BIOSes.

services.name: Read sectors (CHS)
in: sector 1-63 in bits 5:0, cylinder bits 9:8 in bits 7:6
quirks: The buffer must not cross a 64 KiB physical boundary (status 09h) on floppy DMA.
Some BIOSes cannot cross a track or head boundary in one call; read a track at a time.
Sectors count from 1, cylinders and heads from 0.

services.name: Write sectors (CHS)
in: sector 1-63 in bits 5:0, cylinder bits 9:8 in bits 7:6
quirks: Same 64 KiB DMA boundary rule as AH=02h.

services.name: Verify sectors (CHS)
in: sector in bits 5:0, cylinder bits 9:8 in bits 7:6

services.name: Get drive parameters
out: maximum sector in bits 5:0, maximum cylinder bits 9:8 in bits 7:6
quirks: Values are maxima: heads = DH + 1, cylinders = max cylinder + 1, sectors per track = CL & 3Fh.
Set ES:DI = 0000:0000 first; some BIOSes leave it unchanged for hard disks, others need it for floppies.
DL returns the drive count, overwriting the drive number.

services.name: Get disk type
out: 00h no drive, 01h floppy without change line, 02h floppy with change line, 03h hard disk
quirks: On success AH is the disk type, not a status code: do not test AH = 0 for success.

services.name: Check extensions present
out: interface bitmap: bit 0 extended access (42h-44h, 47h, 48h), bit 1 removable drive control, bit 2 EDD (48h DPTE, 4Eh)
quirks: Require CF clear and BX = AA55h and CX bit 0: some BIOSes return CF clear without the extensions.
Some BIOSes report support for floppies (DL < 80h) and then fail AH=42h.

services.name: Extended read
quirks: The DAP and the buffer must be in real-mode-addressable memory (below 1 MiB, reached through DS:SI and segment:offset).
Many BIOSes limit one call to 127 (7Fh) blocks; some fail anything that crosses a 64 KiB buffer boundary.
The BIOS rewrites the DAP count with the blocks transferred: reset it before retrying.

services.name: Extended write
in: 00h/01h write without verify, 02h write with verify
quirks: Same memory and block-count rules as AH=42h.

services.name: Get extended drive parameters
in: result buffer, size word set (1Ah, 1Eh or 42h)
quirks: Set the buffer's size word first; some BIOSes write the full EDD 3.0 structure regardless, so allocate 4Ah bytes.

services.name: Bootable CD-ROM emulation status / terminate
quirks: Some BIOSes need DL = the CD drive number rather than the emulated one.
services.confidence: AL meaning per El Torito 1.0; a few BIOSes implement only AL=01h

services.name: Initialize serial port
in: bits 7:5 baud (000=110 ... 111=9600), 4:3 parity, 2 stop bits, 1:0 word length
quirks: Only up to 9600 baud: program the UART directly for anything faster.

services.name: Disable A20 gate
quirks: Not every BIOS implements the A20 functions: on CF set with AH = 86h fall back to the keyboard controller or port 92h.

services.name: Enable A20 gate
quirks: Verify with a wrap test (compare 0000:0500 with FFFF:0510) afterwards; some BIOSes return success without enabling A20.
Fall back to port 92h or the keyboard controller on CF set.

services.name: Query A20 gate status
out: set by some BIOSes (keyboard controller retries)

services.name: Keyboard intercept
quirks: Called by the INT 09h handler, not by programs: hook it to filter scan codes.

services.name: APM installation check
out: flags: bit 0 16-bit pmode supported, bit 1 32-bit pmode supported, bit 3 APM disabled

services.name: APM set power state
quirks: Power off (CX = 3) needs an APM 1.2 connection: call AX=530Eh first.

services.name: Wait
services.if: enables interrupts while waiting: it counts RTC periodic interrupts (IRQ 8)
quirks: Resolution is the RTC period, 976 us; short waits round up.
CF set means a wait is already in progress.
Needs IRQ 8 unmasked and working; hangs when the RTC interrupt is masked.

services.name: Move extended memory block
services.if: interrupts are disabled during the move; timer ticks can be lost on long moves
quirks: The BIOS switches to protected mode and back (through a CPU reset on a 286, shutdown code 09h); the A20 state afterwards is BIOS-dependent.
Moves of odd byte counts are impossible: CX counts words.
services.confidence: A20 state on return varies between BIOSes

services.name: Get extended memory size
out: KiB of contiguous memory above 1 MiB
quirks: Capped at 15 MiB (3C00h) on many BIOSes and at 64 MiB by the 16-bit result; use E820h or E801h first.
Some BIOSes do not set CF on failure and return AX = 0.

services.name: Switch to protected mode
in: GDT with eight descriptors (dummy, GDT, IDT, DS, ES, SS, CS, BIOS CS)
quirks: Returns in 16-bit protected mode with the caller's descriptors; rarely implemented correctly, not used by modern loaders.
services.confidence: descriptor list order per the IBM AT reference

services.name: Get system configuration
quirks: AH = 86h with CF set when unsupported.

services.name: Get memory size for >64M configurations
out: KiB between 1 MiB and 16 MiB (at most 3C00h)
configured KiB between 1 MiB and 16 MiB
quirks: Some BIOSes return the values in CX/DX and zeros in AX/BX, others the reverse: use CX/DX when AX and BX are both 0.
Stops at the first memory hole below 4 GiB; prefer E820h.

services.name: Query system address map
in: continuation value (0 on the first call)
buffer size, at least 20 (24 for the ACPI 3.0 attributes)
out: continuation value for the next call; 0 after the last entry
quirks: Check EAX = 'SMAP' after every call; a BIOS without E820h returns something else.
The end is EBX = 0 on most BIOSes and CF set on others: accept either, and treat CF set on the first call as unsupported.
Reload EDX = 'SMAP' and ECX before every call: some BIOSes clobber them.
EBX is opaque: pass back exactly what was returned and do not modify it between calls.
Entries can be unsorted, overlapping or zero-length; sanitise before use.
The buffer must be real-mode addressable.

services.name: Get memory size for >64M configurations (32-bit)
out: configured KiB between 1 MiB and 16 MiB

services.name: Read keystroke
services.if: enables interrupts while waiting for a key
quirks: Blocks until a key is available. Extended keys on 101-key keyboards are translated; use AH=10h to see them.

services.name: Check for keystroke
quirks: Does not remove the key from the buffer: follow with AH=00h.
Some BIOSes enable interrupts during the call.

services.name: Read extended keystroke
out: ASCII character, or E0h for extended keys
services.if: enables interrupts while waiting for a key

services.name: Print character
services.errNote: AH bit 0 = timeout, bit 3 = I/O error, bit 5 = out of paper.

services.name: Get printer status
out: printer status: bit 0 timeout, 3 I/O error, 4 selected, 5 out of paper, 6 acknowledge, 7 not busy

services.name: Boot failure / ROM BASIC
quirks: IBM PCs started Cassette BASIC; later BIOSes print a no-boot-device message or, with BBS, try the next boot device. A boot sector calls it to say "not bootable, try the next one".

services.name: Bootstrap loader
quirks: Reloads the boot sector to 0000:7C00 and jumps to it without resetting hardware or restoring hooked vectors; a reset through 0xCF9 or the keyboard controller is more reliable for a reboot.

services.name: Read system timer ticks
out: non-zero if midnight passed since the last read
quirks: Reading clears the midnight flag, which DOS uses to advance the date.

services.name: Read RTC time
services.errNote: CF set when the clock is not running or an update is in progress; retry.

services.name: PCI BIOS installation check
in: 0 (some BIOSes return the protected-mode entry here)
out: hardware mechanism: bit 0 config mechanism #1, bit 1 #2, bit 4 special cycles via #1, bit 5 via #2
quirks: Require CF clear, AH = 0 and EDX = 'PCI '; the 32-bit registers mean a 386 or later.
Some BIOSes destroy the high halves of 32-bit registers they do not return.
